data.summary: Congruent triangles are the same shape and size. Similar triangles have the same shape with corresponding sides in proportion.
key_concepts: Congruence tests: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS (state the test used)
Similarity tests: AAA (two equal angles suffice), SSS sides proportional, SAS sides proportional with included equal angle
Congruent uses the symbol ≡; similar figures share shape but not necessarily size

formulas.label: Length scale factor
formulas.expression: k = corresponding length on larger / corresponding length on smaller

formulas.label: Area and volume scaling
formulas.expression: area ratio = k^2; volume ratio = k^3
formulas.note: Already standard for similar figures; square/cube the length factor.

worked_examples.question: State which congruence rule applies when two triangles have two equal sides and the included equal angle.
steps: Two corresponding sides equal with the included angle equal

worked_examples.question: Two similar solids have heights 4 cm and 10 cm. The smaller has volume 32 cm^3. Find the volume of the larger.

common_mistakes.fix: AAA proves similarity, not congruence; sizes may differ.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using the length scale factor directly for area or volume.
common_mistakes.fix: Square it for area and cube it for volume.

exam_tips: Sketch both triangles the same way round before pairing sides.
In proofs, name the triangles in corresponding vertex order and state the test (e.g. SAS).
